question: In covering a distance of 30 km, Anmol takes 7 hours more than Nikhil. If Anmol doubles his speed, then he would take 8 hours less than Nikhil. Anmol's speed is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio of Anmol = 1 : 2

Time ratio of Anmol = 2 : 1 (Difference = 1 unit)

Total time saved by doubling speed = 7 hrs (late) + 8 hrs (early) = 15 hrs

1 unit = 15 hrs ⇒ Original time (2 units) = 30 hrs

Anmol's speed = Distance ÷ Time = 30 ÷ 30 = 1 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 1 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Distance = 30 km

Anmol takes 7 hours more than Nikhil initially.

If Anmol doubles his speed, he takes 8 hours less than Nikhil.

 
 
• 
 
 
 Distance = 30 km
 Normal speed time → t + 7 hrs
 Double speed time → t − 8 hrs
 
• 
 Anmol's total time difference = 15 hrs

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

Let the original time taken by Anmol be tₐ and by Nikhil be tₙ.

⇒ tₐ − tₙ = 7 ... (i)

When Anmol's speed is doubled, his new time becomes tₐ ÷ 2.

⇒ tₙ − (tₐ ÷ 2) = 8 ... (ii)

Adding equations (i) and (ii):

⇒ tₐ − (tₐ ÷ 2) = 7 + 8

⇒ tₐ ÷ 2 = 15

⇒ tₐ = 30 hours

Anmol's original speed = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ Speed = 30 ÷ 30 = 1 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 1 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed and Time Inverse Relation

When the distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time. If speed becomes *n* times, the required time becomes *1/n* times.

Average Speed

Average speed is the ratio of total distance traveled to total time taken. For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their speeds. In opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds.
